one_liner: Business chat and collaboration platform (channels, DMs, workflows) with a large Web API surface.
access_note: Anyone can create a Slack app and get bot/user tokens for free via api.slack.com; installing into a third-party workspace still needs that workspace's admin/OAuth approval.
api_breadth_note: Web API covers messaging, channels, users, files, canvases, admin, and workflow automation across hundreds of methods and scopes.
existing_mcp_note: Slack launched an official Slack-hosted remote MCP server (GA Feb 2026) with OAuth2 and admin approval flow.

evidence.note: Official auth overview: OAuth2 flow and token types.
Official Slack MCP server guide confirming Slack-hosted remote MCP with OAuth.

researcher_notes: The official MCP server is a Slack-hosted remote server behind an org admin approval flow, distinct from the classic self-hosted app/bot-token integration path.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform (SMS, voice, video, email) exposed via REST APIs across 30+ products.
access_note: Free self-serve signup grants trial credit and immediate API key/Account SID + Auth Token generation from the Console.
api_breadth_note: Twilio's own MCP announcement cites over 1,800 REST endpoints across 30+ products.
existing_mcp_note: Official Twilio MCP server (twilio-labs/mcp) exposing the full API surface as MCP tools.

evidence.note: Official docs on API key creation and Basic Auth usage.

researcher_notes: Twilio is one of the most agent-ready APIs researched, with an official first-party MCP server already in production use.

one_liner: Team chat app with a low-code developer platform (bots, webhooks, functions) and a REST API.
access_note: Free Zoho sign-up gives access to the Cliq developer platform; webhook tokens (zapikey) and OAuth client credentials are both self-generated at no cost.
api_breadth_note: REST API v2/v3 covers messages, bots, channels, and functions.
existing_mcp_note: Zoho published an official Zoho Cliq MCP Server as part of the broader Zoho MCP suite.

evidence.note: Official REST API v3 messages reference.
Official Zoho Cliq MCP server guide.

researcher_notes: Two parallel auth surfaces exist (webhook tokens vs OAuth2) — worth checking which the MCP server uses.

one_liner: All-in-one collaboration suite (chat, docs, calendar, approvals) from ByteDance with an extensive Open Platform API.
access_note: Free registration at open.larksuite.com yields an App ID/Secret used to self-generate app/tenant/user access tokens without sales contact.
api_breadth_note: Open Platform covers messaging, docs, sheets, calendar, contacts, approvals, and more.
existing_mcp_note: Official Lark/Feishu OpenAPI MCP server at github.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp.

evidence.note: Official server-side docs on obtaining app/tenant access tokens.

researcher_notes: Documentation is bilingual (Feishu domestic vs Lark international) and can be confusing to navigate.

one_liner: Free team chat app (Slack alternative) with a REST API add-on for messaging, channels, and reactions.
access_note: The API add-on is installable and API keys generated directly in-app on all plans including the Free workspace tier.
api_breadth_note: Covers a limited action set — sending/replying/deleting messages, reactions, channel creation, and listing messages/channels.
existing_mcp_note: Community/third-party Pumble MCP server and a Zapier-hosted Pumble MCP integration; no official Pumble-built MCP found.

evidence.note: Official help doc confirming API add-on is available on all plans including Free.

researcher_notes: The API is an 'add-on' built by CAKE.com (Pumble's parent) rather than a first-party core API.

one_liner: Community chat platform (text/voice/video) with a REST + Gateway API for building bots and apps.
access_note: Free registration at discord.com/developers/applications gives an instant bot token and OAuth2 client credentials, no approval needed for most scopes.
api_breadth_note: Covers messaging, channels, guild/server management, moderation, webhooks, and real-time events via REST plus a WebSocket Gateway.
existing_mcp_note: Multiple community MCP servers exist; no official Discord-built MCP server found.

evidence.note: Official OAuth2 and bot token authentication documentation.
Example community Discord MCP server for Claude integration.

researcher_notes: Verified-bot requirements and message-content intent approval can gate certain bot capabilities at scale.

one_liner: Messaging app with a free public Bot API for automated messaging, plus a separate MTProto API for full user-account access.
access_note: Bot tokens are issued instantly and free via @BotFather; the lower-level MTProto user API requires a free api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org.
api_breadth_note: The HTTP/JSON Bot API covers messaging, media, inline queries, and updates well, but lacks full client capabilities available only via MTProto.
existing_mcp_note: Several community MCP servers exist; none official from Telegram.

evidence.note: Official Bot API reference confirming free token-based HTTPS/JSON access.

researcher_notes: Bot API and user-account (MTProto) access are two very different integration paths with different auth and capability sets.

one_liner: Meta's business messaging platform; the Cloud API lets developers programmatically send/receive WhatsApp messages.
access_note: A free Test Business Account allows immediate messaging to up to 5 verified numbers, but production use at scale requires Meta Business verification (documents, 2-10 business day review).
api_breadth_note: Cloud API covers messaging (text, media, templates, interactive), phone number registration, and Business Account management endpoints.
existing_mcp_note: Multiple unofficial MCP servers exist, some wrapping the official Cloud API; no official Meta-built MCP found.
main_blocker: Full production access requires Meta Business verification/approval; unverified test mode is capped at 250 conversations/24h and 5 numbers.

evidence.note: Official docs on registering a developer and test webhook setup.

researcher_notes: 'Free' framing is misleading — prototyping is free and self-serve, but real deployment needs Meta Business verification.

one_liner: Cloud-based business phone system / call center software with a REST API and webhooks for calls, contacts, and SMS.
access_note: API keys are generated from Company Settings, which requires an active paid Aircall subscription (no free tier exists for the product itself).
api_breadth_note: REST API covers calls, contacts, users, teams, SMS, WhatsApp, AI call summaries/transcripts, and webhooks.
existing_mcp_note: Unofficial community MCP server; Aircall's own docs list official MCP-compliant integrations as 'Coming soon'.
main_blocker: Requires being a paying Aircall customer (Basic Auth uses api_id/api_token issued only to subscribed accounts) to obtain API credentials.

evidence.note: Official developer portal, confirms REST API + webhooks and that MCP tooling is 'Coming soon'.

researcher_notes: Aircall is actively building first-party MCP/AI-agent support per their own dev portal roadmap.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform (SMS, Voice, Video, Verify/2FA) with REST APIs and free trial credit for developers.
access_note: Free self-serve account creation yields an API key/secret and trial credit immediately, but trial mode restricts calls/SMS to up to 5 verified test numbers until upgraded.
api_breadth_note: Covers SMS, Voice, Video, Verify, Number Insight, Messages API, and Application management.
existing_mcp_note: Vonage publishes an official Documentation MCP server and a Vonage-Community telephony MCP server.

evidence.note: Official docs on Basic Auth (API key/secret) and JWT authentication.
Official Vonage blog introducing their Documentation MCP server.

researcher_notes: Vonage has multiple distinct MCP servers (docs-lookup vs telephony-tools) — worth confirming ownership before relying on 'official' status.
